entries.1:1: The writer is talking about Jesus, who existed from the very beginning and whom the writers actually saw, heard, and touched. This means the message about Jesus is based on real, firsthand experience, not made-up stories.
entries.1:2: The life they are talking about is Jesus, who was with God the Father and then appeared to people. The writers saw him themselves and are now telling others about him so they can know this eternal life too.
entries.1:3: The writers are sharing what they saw and heard so that their readers can share the same close friendship with God and Jesus that they have. Being a Christian means being joined together with God and with other believers.
entries.1:4: The writer is writing this letter so that both he and his readers can have complete joy. Knowing the truth about Jesus and sharing it brings full happiness.
entries.1:5: The message they heard from Jesus is simple: God is pure light, and there is nothing evil or hidden in him at all. This means God is completely good and trustworthy.
entries.1:6: If we claim to be close to God but keep living in sin and darkness, we are lying and not living by the truth. What we say about our faith has to match how we actually live.
entries.1:7: If we live in the light, the way God does, we have real fellowship with each other, and Jesus' death cleanses us from every sin. Living honestly before God brings us together and keeps us clean.
entries.1:8: If we claim we have never sinned, we are fooling ourselves and the truth is not in us. Admitting we are sinners is the honest starting point for receiving God's forgiveness.
entries.1:9: Confess and he forgives and cleanses, fully. Confession is not begging; it is a promise being kept.
entries.1:10: If we say we have never sinned, we are calling God a liar and showing that his message has no place in us. Denying our sin keeps us from the truth and from God's grace.
entries.2:1: John writes so his readers will avoid sin, but he also reassures them that if they do sin, Jesus stands with them before God as their helper. You can take comfort that failure doesn't cut you off from God's help.
entries.2:2: Jesus' death paid for our sins, and not just ours but the sins of the whole world. God's forgiveness is offered far more widely than just to you and your group.
entries.2:3: We can know we truly know God if we actually do what he commands. Claiming to know God means little unless your actions back it up.
entries.2:4: Anyone who says they know God but ignores his commands is lying to themselves. Words of faith don't count if your life doesn't match them.
entries.2:5: When someone keeps God's word, God's love reaches its full expression in them. Obeying God is how you can be sure you really belong to him.
entries.2:6: If you claim to live in Jesus, you should live the way he lived. Your claim is only real if your everyday behavior follows his example.
entries.2:7: John isn't giving a brand-new command but the old one his readers have heard from the start. What God asks of you isn't some fresh secret; it's the same message you already know.
entries.2:8: Still, this command is new in the sense that it's coming true in Jesus and in you, as darkness fades and real light shines. You are living in a time when the light is breaking through.
entries.2:9: Anyone who claims to be in the light but hates their brother is still in darkness. How you treat others shows whether you're really walking in God's light.
entries.2:10: Whoever loves their brother stays in the light and won't stumble. Loving others keeps you steady and keeps you from going wrong.
entries.2:11: Someone who hates their brother is lost in the dark and doesn't know where they're going because the darkness has blinded them. Hatred clouds your judgment and leads you astray.
entries.2:12: John writes to his readers because their sins are forgiven through Jesus. You can be confident your sins are forgiven because of him.
entries.2:13: John addresses different groups: older believers who have known God from the beginning, younger ones who have beaten the Evil One, and children who know the Father. Whatever your stage of life, there's something true about your standing with God.
entries.2:14: John repeats his encouragement to fathers and young men, adding that the young are strong because God's word lives in them and they have overcome the Evil One. God's word in you gives you real strength against evil.
entries.2:15: Don't set your heart on the world and its things, because loving the world crowds out love for the Father. What you love most shapes who you belong to.
entries.2:16: The cravings of the body, the craving for what you see, and pride in what you have all come from the world, not from the Father. These desires don't come from God, so don't treat them as your guide.
entries.2:17: The world and its desires are passing away, but whoever does God's will lives forever. Invest your life in what lasts rather than in what is fading.
entries.2:18: John says this is the last hour, and just as people were warned an antichrist would come, many false opponents of Christ have already appeared. You should be alert, because the signs of the end are already here.
entries.2:19: Those false teachers left the community, which shows they never really belonged to it. If they had been truly part of it, they would have stayed, and their leaving makes that clear.
entries.2:20: You have received the Spirit from the Holy One, so you all have knowledge. God has given you what you need to know the truth.
entries.2:21: John isn't writing because his readers lack knowledge of the truth, but because they have it, and because lies have nothing in common with truth. You can trust what you already know to be true.
entries.2:22: The liar is the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ; such a person is the antichrist, denying both the Father and the Son. Rejecting who Jesus is means rejecting God himself.
entries.2:23: Anyone who denies the Son doesn't have the Father either, but whoever acknowledges the Son has the Father too. You can't have God the Father while rejecting his Son.
entries.2:24: Keep in your hearts what you were taught from the beginning; if you do, you will remain in the Father and the Son. Hold on to the core message you first received.
entries.2:25: The promise Jesus gave you is eternal life. What God offers you is life that never ends.
entries.2:26: John writes these things because some people are trying to lead his readers away from the truth. Be aware that some will try to pull you off the right path.
entries.2:27: The Spirit you received stays in you, so you don't need anyone else to teach you; his teaching is true, so remain in him. Trust the Spirit's guidance and stay close to God.
entries.2:28: Stay close to Jesus so that when he appears, you can face him without fear or shame. Living faithfully now means confidence when he comes.
entries.2:29: Since you know God is righteous, you also know that everyone who does what is right is his child. Right living shows whose family you belong to.
entries.3:1: God's love is so great that he calls us his own children, and that is truly what we are. It means you can be confident you belong to God's family, even when others don't understand it.
entries.3:2: We are already God's children, though we don't yet know fully what we will become; one day we will see Jesus and be like him. It means your future with God is secure and better than anything you can picture now.
entries.3:3: Anyone who hopes to see Jesus and be like him works at living a pure and holy life. It means your hope should show up in how you live each day.
entries.3:4: Sin is simply breaking God's law. It means wrong choices are not small matters; they are going against what God has said.
entries.3:5: Jesus came to remove sin, and there was no sin in him at all. It means he is the one who can truly clean you up and set you free.
entries.3:6: Someone who keeps living in sin has not really come to know Jesus. It means a real relationship with him changes how you live, not just what you say.
entries.3:7: Don't let anyone mislead you: the person who does what is right shows they are right with God, just as Jesus is right. It means your actions reveal whether your faith is real.
entries.3:8: Sin belongs to the devil, who has been sinning from the start, and Jesus came to destroy the devil's work. It means sin is not your friend, and Jesus has the power to break it in your life.
entries.3:9: Someone born of God does not keep on sinning, because God's life is in them. It means God's presence in you makes a real difference in how you live.
entries.3:10: You can tell God's children from the devil's children by whether they do right and love their fellow believers. It means loving others is a clear sign of whose family you belong to.
entries.3:11: From the very beginning we were told to love one another. It means love for others is not optional; it is the core of what we were taught.
entries.3:12: Don't be like Cain, who killed his brother because his own deeds were evil and his brother's were good. It means jealousy and hatred can lead people to terrible things, so guard your heart.
entries.3:13: Don't be shocked when the world hates you. It means opposition to your faith is normal, not a sign that something is wrong with you.
entries.3:14: We know we have moved from death to life because we love our brothers and sisters; anyone without love is still in death. It means loving others is evidence that you are truly alive in God.
entries.3:15: Anyone who hates his brother is a murderer at heart, and no murderer has eternal life in him. It means hatred is serious to God, so deal with it before it grows.
entries.3:16: We learn what love is from Jesus, who gave his life for us, and we should be willing to give our lives for others. It means real love is sacrificial, not just a feeling.
entries.3:17: If you have enough to live on and see a brother in need but shut your heart to him, God's love can't be in you. It means your generosity toward those in need shows whether God's love is real in you.
entries.3:18: Don't love only with words and talk; love with actions and in truth. It means show your love by what you actually do, not just what you say.
entries.3:19: This is how we can know we belong to the truth and set our hearts at rest before God. It means loving in action gives you confidence that your faith is genuine.
entries.3:20: When your heart condemns you, remember that God is greater than your heart and knows everything. It means you can trust God's judgment over your own guilty feelings.
entries.3:21: If our heart does not condemn us, we can come to God without fear. It means a clear conscience gives you boldness and peace before him.
entries.3:22: We receive what we ask from God because we keep his commands and do what pleases him. It means living God's way keeps your prayers in line with his will.
entries.3:23: His command is that we believe in Jesus Christ and love one another. It means faith in Jesus and love for people are the two things God asks of us.
entries.3:24: Whoever keeps God's commands lives in God and God lives in him, and the Spirit he gave us confirms this. It means you can know God is with you through the Spirit he has placed in you.
entries.4:1: Not everyone who claims to speak for God is really from him, so test what they say. Check teachings against the truth instead of believing them just because they sound spiritual.
entries.4:2: A teacher truly from God will affirm that Jesus Christ actually came as a real human being. That confession is the test that separates God's Spirit from error.
entries.4:3: Anyone who denies that Jesus came in the flesh is not speaking from God but from the spirit of falsehood opposed to Christ. Such teaching was already spreading, so be on guard against it.
entries.4:4: You belong to God and have already overcome these false teachers, because God's Spirit in you is stronger than the spirit at work in the world. You need not be afraid of deceptive voices.
entries.4:5: False teachers speak the world's language and the world listens to them because they belong to it. Don't be surprised when the world embraces messages that deny Christ.
entries.4:6: Those who truly know God listen to the apostolic teaching, while those who don't belong to God reject it. This is how you can tell the Spirit of truth from the spirit of error.
entries.4:7: Love one another, because love comes from God and marks everyone who is truly his child. If you know God, love for others should be a natural part of your life.
entries.4:8: God is love, so a life without love does not know him. Love is evidence, not just sentiment.
entries.4:9: God showed his love by sending his one and only Son into the world so that we could have life through him. His love is not just a feeling but an action that gives us life.
entries.4:10: Real love began with God, not with us: he loved us first and sent his Son to deal with our sins. We don't earn his love; we receive it.
entries.4:11: Since God loved us that much, we should love one another too. His love for us should shape how we treat other people.
entries.4:12: No one has seen God, but when we love one another, God lives in us and his love reaches its full expression in us. Your love for others makes the invisible God visible.
entries.4:13: God's Spirit, which he has given us, assures us that we live in him and he lives in us. You can know you belong to God because his Spirit is within you.
entries.4:14: We have seen and testify that the Father sent the Son to be the Savior of the world. This is the good news we are called to share with others.
entries.4:15: Whoever openly confesses that Jesus is the Son of God has God living in him and lives in God. Speaking that truth is more than words; it marks a real relationship with God.
entries.4:16: We have come to know and trust the love God has for us, because God is love and those who live in love live in him. Trusting his love changes how you live.
entries.4:17: God's love is brought to full maturity in us so we can face the day of judgment without fear, because in this world we are like Jesus. Living in his love gives you confidence rather than dread.
entries.4:18: Perfect love drives out fear, because fear involves punishment and shows love isn't yet complete. The more you rest in God's love, the less you need to be afraid.
entries.4:19: We love because he loved us first. Our love is a response, never the starting point.
entries.4:20: Anyone who claims to love God but hates his brother is lying, since you can't love the God you haven't seen while hating the brother you have seen. Love for God must show up in how you treat people around you.
entries.4:21: God's command is simple: whoever loves God must also love his brother. Loving God and loving others go together and can't be separated.
entries.5:1: Believing that Jesus is the promised Savior makes you part of God's family. If you love God as your Father, you will also love his children, the people who belong to him.
entries.5:2: We can know we truly love God's people when we love God himself and do what he commands. Love for God and love for others go together.
entries.5:3: Loving God shows itself in obeying what he says, and his commands are not a crushing burden. Following him is meant to be possible, not impossible.
entries.5:4: Everything that comes from God can win the victory over the world's pull away from him. The way we win that victory is by trusting God.
entries.5:5: The only person who can truly overcome the world is the one who believes Jesus is God's Son. That faith is what makes the difference.
entries.5:6: Jesus came with both water and blood, meaning his whole mission from baptism to death was real. He did not come in part only but fully.
entries.5:7: The Holy Spirit also testifies about Jesus, and the Spirit can be trusted because he is truth. God himself confirms who Jesus is.
entries.5:8: The Spirit, the water, and the blood all agree in pointing to Jesus. Their testimony lines up as one consistent witness.
entries.5:9: If we accept human testimony, God's testimony about his Son is far greater. What God says about Jesus carries more weight than anything people say.
entries.5:10: Whoever believes in God's Son has that testimony living inside them. Whoever refuses to believe is calling God a liar about his own Son.
entries.5:11: God's testimony is that he has given us eternal life, and that life is found in his Son. You receive that life by having the Son.
entries.5:12: Whoever has the Son has real life; whoever does not have the Son does not have that life. It all hinges on your connection to Jesus.
entries.5:13: John wrote these things so that believers could be sure they have eternal life. You do not have to live in doubt about where you stand with God.
entries.5:14: We can be confident that if we ask for something that matches what God wants, he hears us. Prayer is not wishful thinking but a real conversation with a listening God.
entries.5:15: Since we know he hears every request that is in line with his will, we can know he will answer. You can pray with confidence, not fear.
entries.5:16: If you see a fellow believer sinning in a way that does not lead to death, you should pray, and God can give them life. There is a kind of sin that leads to death, and John does not tell us to pray about that one.
entries.5:17: Every wrong thing done is sin, but not every sin carries the same deadly consequence. Sin is always serious, yet not all sin ends in death.
entries.5:18: A child of God does not keep on sinning as a way of life, because God's Son protects them from the Evil One. You are guarded, not left on your own.
entries.5:19: We know we belong to God, but the rest of the world is under the Evil One's control. This helps you understand why the world so often opposes God.
entries.5:20: We know God's Son has come and has opened our eyes to know the true God, and we live in him through Jesus. Jesus is the true God and the source of eternal life.
entries.5:21: John ends by telling his dear readers to stay away from false gods. Anything that takes God's rightful place in your life is worth guarding against.
